A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same IRIS system and CWE-Bench-Java study. All 24 pages of each version, including figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–D, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports original vulnerability-detection experiments, manual specification assessments, component ablations, and runtime measurements.

after.justification: V3 retains these original empirical results and adds results for two further IRIS model configurations.

M1.justification: The four-stage IRIS procedure and prompt/query listings are retained. Appendix A.3 explains existing prompting and path truncation choices, including previously unspecified sampling details; it does not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 120 Java vulnerabilities across CWE-22, CWE-78, CWE-79, and CWE-94, plus the investigation of 30 projects for unknown vulnerabilities. Additional model configurations and error discussion do not introduce new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated static-analysis comparators remain CodeQL, Facebook Infer, SpotBugs, and Snyk, with unchanged membership in the corresponding comparisons. The additional LLMs are configurations of IRIS rather than new competing detection methods.

E3.justification: Table 1 adds IRIS evaluations with Qwen-2.5-Coder 32B and Gemma-2 27B. Appendix C.1 stops listing DeepSeekCoder 33B, Mistral 7B, and Gemma 7B, for which v2 supplied no separate result rows. Dataset size, metrics, CodeQL version, and decoding settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix C.7 adds qualitative error analysis, including CVE-2020-11977 and failures involving missing dataflow connections or specifications. This supplies a concrete missed-vulnerability example without a quantified error breakdown. Existing source/sink ablations, contextual-analysis comparisons, and specification analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the fixed-seed statement for GPT models and the same manual sampling descriptions. Neither introduces additional repeated-run reporting, confidence intervals, or significance testing; the added model rows follow the existing reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds Qwen-2.5-Coder results of 47 detections, 92.38% FDR, and 0.097 F1, and Gemma-2 results of 45 detections, 91.23% FDR, and 0.100 F1. Existing rows remain unchanged. Section 5.3 changes six potential unknown vulnerabilities, four reported, to four vulnerabilities and corrects CWE-94's description to code injection. V2's detailed alert/report/confirmation statistics are removed.

T1.justification: The graph, taint-specification, unsanitized-path, and evaluation-metric definitions remain substantively identical. Notation corrections and revised explanations introduce no new mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction reduce the claimed number of previously unknown vulnerabilities from six to four, and the introduction changes the stated LLM count from eight to seven. The central neuro-symbolic contribution, 120-vulnerability benchmark, and GPT-4 result of 55 detections versus CodeQL's 27 remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendices A.3 and C.7 add context-length cost/accuracy reasoning and more specific explanations of detection failures. Conversely, v3 removes the qualification that newly reported vulnerabilities await developer confirmation, without supplying replacement confirmation evidence. The conclusion's general limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V3 replaces the supplementary-material/future-release statement with reported public code and dataset access links, adds the two new model IDs, and documents S=10 with segmented path sampling that favors function calls. The five-line context window was already specified in v2. Documentation of the custom triage interface and vulnerability-reporting process is removed.

R1.justification: Section 6 adds an explicit comparison with InspectJS and references to Hoppity, general query engines, and LLMDFA, while removing the AutoCodeRover/SWE-Agent discussion. These locally broaden positioning without changing the main whole-project neuro-symbolic contribution. Bibliographic corrections and citation-style changes are not substantive additions.

P1.justification: V3 adds IRIS to the title, acknowledgments, localized prose revisions, and author-year citations. Appendix subsections are added and reorganized, while the unknown-vulnerability appendix subsection is removed. The main section order and most explanatory prose remain intact.

P2.justification: V3 adopts ICLR headers and typography, adjusts figure/table placement and listing layout, expands Tables 1 and 6, and reformats Table 5. V2's Table 7 and interface screenshot, Figure 11, are removed. Figures 1–10 and most existing table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: The documented path-sampling procedure, public artifact access information, and concrete failure analysis make IRIS easier to reproduce and assess; Table 1 also extends evidence across model configurations. These are incremental gains to an otherwise stable paper. They are partly offset by removal of v2's pending-confirmation disclosure and status table, which makes the revised four-vulnerability claim less transparent.
